key.title: Thought and Character
key.main_idea: Your character is the sum of your thoughts. Every action grows from thoughts the way a plant grows from a seed, so by watching and changing what you think, you shape who you become and, over time, your circumstances.

key_lessons.text: You are, quite literally, what you think: your character is the total of your thoughts.
key_lessons.source_snippet: his character being the complete sum of all his thoughts

key_lessons.text: Every action grows from a hidden seed of thought, even the ones that seem spontaneous.
key_lessons.source_snippet: every act of a man springs from the hidden seeds of thought

key_lessons.text: Good character is not luck. It is the result of steady effort in right thinking.
key_lessons.source_snippet: is not a thing of favour or chance, but is the natural result of continued effort in right thinking

key_lessons.text: You are the master of your thoughts, so you hold the key to every situation.
key_lessons.source_snippet: man holds the key to every situation

key_lessons.text: Self-knowledge comes from patient practice: watch your thoughts, notice their effects, and change them.
key_lessons.source_snippet: if he will watch, control, and alter his thoughts

key.takeaway: Watch your thoughts the way a gardener watches seeds. What you think about every day is slowly becoming who you are.

quick_check.question: According to James Allen, where does a person's character come from?
options: From the total of their thoughts
Only from the actions others see
quick_check.simpler_explanation: Allen says thoughts are like seeds. Actions grow from them, and over time those thoughts and actions become your character. So character is built from what you think, not given by chance.

reflection_questions: Which thought have you repeated so often this month that it now feels like part of you?
Think of one recent action you did "without thinking". What thought might have been behind it?
Which one thought would you most like to replace, and with what?

complete.title: Thought and Character
complete.main_idea: Your character is the sum of your thoughts. Every action grows from thoughts the way a plant grows from a seed, so by watching and changing what you think, you shape who you become and, over time, your circumstances.

sections.heading: "As a man thinketh"
sections.explanation: Allen opens with the old saying, "As a man thinketh in his heart so is he," and takes it literally: a person is what they think. Their character is the complete sum of their thoughts, and this reaches into every part of life.

sections.heading: Thoughts are seeds
sections.explanation: Just as a plant cannot exist without a seed, no action can appear without a thought behind it. This is true even of actions we call spontaneous. Action is the flower; joy and suffering are the fruit we later harvest.

examples.text: The seed-and-blossom picture is Allen's own.
examples.source_snippet: Act is the blossom of thought, and joy and suffering are its fruits

sections.heading: Character is grown, not given
sections.explanation: A noble character is not a gift of luck. It grows from long effort in right thinking, just as a poor character grows from repeatedly harbouring low thoughts. Cause and effect work as firmly in the mind as in the physical world.

examples.text: He states that good character is "not a thing of favour or chance".
examples.source_snippet: is not a thing of favour or chance, but is the natural result of continued effort in right thinking

sections.heading: You are the master
sections.explanation: Allen calls this the most hopeful truth of all: each of us is the master of thought and the maker of character. Even at our weakest we are still the master, only a foolish one who mismanages the "household". Reflection turns us into wise masters.

examples.text: A person who reacts angrily every morning in traffic can, by noticing the thought "everyone is against me", choose a calmer one. Nothing outside changes, but the day does.

sections.heading: Dig for self-knowledge
sections.explanation: Truth about ourselves is found the way gold and diamonds are: by much searching and mining. Watch, control and change your thoughts, trace their effects on you and others, and use even small daily events as lessons. Patience and practice open the door.

examples.text: Allen's image of mining for gold and diamonds.
examples.source_snippet: Only by much searching and mining, are gold and diamonds obtained
